lines.text: One in two thousand people live with Long QT syndrome. For them, hundreds of everyday medicines can trigger a dangerous heart rhythm.
Meet Celia.ai. A heart-safety companion you can talk to.
The doctor gave me Klacid for a sinus infection.
Klacid is clarithromycin. It's on the known-risk list, so please don't start it before you talk to your doctor.
The verdict comes from fixed medical data. The AI only explains it.
Or scan the box. Sixty-eight thousand Polish packs, checked right on the phone.
Your watch keeps an eye on your heart rate. When something looks off, the agent checks in.
And if you can't answer, it speaks for you. In thirteen languages.
The safety core runs on your phone. And you see everything that leaves it.
Celia.ai. Know before you take it.
One in two thousand people have Long QT syndrome. Everyday medicines can trigger it.
Your watch keeps an eye on your heart rate.
